title: Allow blur() after an element becomes non-focusable
body: Remove the focusability check from the unfocusing steps so that blur() can synchronously unfocus an element that has become non-focusable but is still in the current focus chain. For example, hiding a focused textarea's ancestor and then calling blur() should immediately move focus to the viewport, without waiting for focus fixup during update the rendering. This matches Chromium, Gecko, and WebKit. Discovered while investigating https://github.com/jsdom/jsdom/issues/4431. - [x] At least two implementers are interested (and none opposed): - Matches existing Chromium, Gecko, and WebKit behavior. All three new subtests pass in Chromium 156.0.8078.4, Firefox 157.0, and Playwright WebKit 26.5. - [x] [Tests](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt) are written and can be reviewed and commented upon at: - https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/64336 - [x] [Implementation bugs](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md#handling-pull-requests) are filed: - Chromium: N/A, already implemented. - Gecko: N/A, already implemented. - WebKit: N/A, already implemented. - Deno (only for timers, structured clone, base64 utils, channel messaging, module resolution, web workers, and web storage): N/A - Node.js (only for timers, structured clone, base64 utils, channel messaging, and module resolution): N/A - [x] Corresponding [HTML AAM](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/) & [ARIA in HTML](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/) issues & PRs: N/A - [x] [MDN issue](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md#handling-pull-requests) is filed: N/A, too much of an edge-case. - [x] The top of this comment includes a [clear commit message](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/COMMITTING.md) to use.
